clue.text: Women steering at sea or hoofing it?

definitions.meaning: first reading: young women at the helm of a boat

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the dancers who do it
definitions.meaning: second reading: hoofing is slang for dancing, and this was a famous precision dance troupe

explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a British high-kicking dance troupe, named after founder John Tiller; read literally, the name suggests girls at a boat's tiller.
explanation.definitionFit: The troupe were showbusiness dancers, and a tiller is the lever used to steer a boat.

clue.text: Attila or Tamburlaine, perhaps: of course, he'd g-got a divine means of punishment

indicators.note: the stutter itself suggests words jumbled in the mouth, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written, with the stammered extra G

explanation.surface: A historian muses on the great conquerors and how they came to be seen as heaven's instruments of wrath.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer supplies the second G the anagram needs. The answer is defined at both ends: by the warlords given the title, and by its literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun was called the Scourge of God, a title later applied to Tamburlaine, as a whip sent by heaven to chastise sinners.

clue.text: Force nail back into Chinese measurement

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word nail from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written, then turned around
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Someone hammers a nail home while switching to traditional Chinese units.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is LIAN plus G; 'into' is just a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The liang, also called the tael, is a traditional Chinese unit of weight, roughly an ounce and a third.

clue.text: Unusual collection made when late partner cut one coat

parts.note: a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: cutting cloth into pieces and reworking them suggests the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A divorce story: the ex slashed one of the coats, making a strange heap of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' here means former, not dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or foreign objects, especially as gathered together, so the plural noun names an unusual assortment.

clue.text: Grouse about crook getting the George Cross

indicators.note: about means turned around and moved here and there, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
GC is the abbreviation for the George Cross, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a villain has been awarded a top medal for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like a verb meaning complain; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorcock is the male red grouse, a game bird of British moorland.

clue.text: Wretched fellow on call's got a fungal infection

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting one thing on another can mean adding it onto the end, so the fellow comes second

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
a worm is a contemptible, wretched person

explanation.surface: A pitiable man on a phone call admits he has caught something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: RING then WORM: 'on' here means the fellow is added onto the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious skin disease caused by fungi, not by any worm, producing ring-shaped patches.

clue.text: Like a star, travelling singly round wreck of Titanic with two students

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about and do not stay in their places
a wreck is something smashed apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is learner, a student driver; two of them

explanation.surface: A celebrity voyager sails alone over the sunken liner with a couple of students in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters are mixed together; 'round' only nods at the shape of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A star twinkles and sparkles, and scintillating means giving off flashes of light, so the adverb describes shining that way.

clue.text: Make a confession about advertising some time before the summer

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
public relations, the business of promotion

explanation.surface: A criminal owns up to a publicity stunt a few months before the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of March to May comes directly ahead of the warmest months of the year.

clue.text: Gone back round the child's horse, they say, to get a drink

indicators.note: going back means the word gone is read from end to start
round means one part wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written, then turned around

indicators.note: they say means we take the nursery word as it is spoken

parts.note: gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, written as two letters

explanation.surface: A parent goes back round the toy horse, ready for a festive tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a sweet beverage of eggs, milk and sugar, often laced with rum or brandy at Christmas.

clue.text: It's child's play to look endlessly about

indicators.note: endlessly means the tail of the word about is cut off

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
taken as written, then its end is dropped

explanation.surface: Looking round about you, it's simple enough for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEKABO is a variant spelling of the game; here two letters, not one, go from the end of ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game of hiding the face and revealing it to amuse a baby, literally a pastime for infants.

clue.text: Two kings accepting an order

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the kings hold the other piece inside

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king, and the second king is taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of monarchs receive a royal command or decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the abbreviation of Rex, as on coins and in legal titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a position in a list arranged by grade, so it means an ordering of things.

clue.text: General in command in Northern Ireland going back to Ulster to an assumed identity

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective or adverb, under an assumed identity

indicators.note: going back means the title is read from its end to its start

parts.words: General in command in Northern Ireland
parts.note: GOC NI is the General Officer Commanding Northern Ireland, an army post
Ulster is used for Northern Ireland
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army commander returns to Ulster in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' just joins the clue; the second gives TO. GOC is the standard army abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their real name and appearance, adopting a false persona.

clue.text: Old King's Counsellors providing wit and wisdom

indicators.note: providing means the words supply the letters from within themselves

parts.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding that completes the phrase

explanation.surface: Royal advisers of old offered both humour and good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the council of wise men who advised Anglo-Saxon kings.

clue.text: French good taste can cause pain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French word for taste, as in bon goût

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: Refined French cuisine leads to suffering for the gourmet.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word goût (taste) is spelt the same as the English joint disease, which rich food was blamed for.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout is an inflammation of the joints, especially the big toe, known for being extremely painful.

clue.text: Large farm spread round king's recognition signal

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
spread means laid out loosely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A big agricultural estate stretches all around the monarch's lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker flag is planted or flown to identify a position or boundary, so others can spot it.

clue.text: Siblings who can sometimes be exclusive?

definitions.text: Siblings who can sometimes be exclusive

parts.words: Siblings who can sometimes be exclusive
parts.note: surface reading: brothers and sisters who leave others out
setter's reading: the name of a strict Christian sect that keeps apart from outsiders

explanation.walkthrough: The Exclusive Brethren are a branch of the Plymouth Brethren who keep apart from outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: The old plural of brother is used for fellow members of a religious community.

clue.text: Sounds like the late Vice President's political philosophy has to do with Arabic or decimal counting

definitions.text: has to do with Arabic or decimal counting
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to say the politician's creed and spell what we hear

parts.words: the late Vice President's political philosophy
parts.note: Al Gore was US Vice President; an -ism is a doctrine, and -ic means relating to it

explanation.surface: A pundit links a former American politician's beliefs to arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means former: Al Gore served under Clinton.
explanation.definitionFit: Algorism is the Arabic decimal system of numerals and calculation, so the adjective relates to that arithmetic.

clue.text: Four-bar cadenza containing an overarching passage

indicators.note: containing means the letters sit inside the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A short virtuoso solo in a piece of music includes a sweeping melodic phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' and 'bar' pull towards music, but the definition is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walkway lined by arches, so it is literally a passageway with arches overhead.

clue.text: Peter's confused about 100 staff

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the number
confused means mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bewildered Peter worries about a workforce of a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is an ornamental rod carried by a monarch as an emblem of sovereignty.

clue.text: Cleanly cut: it sounds just the opposite of very large

indicators.note: it sounds tells us the spelling follows a spoken phrase

parts.words: just the opposite of very large
parts.note: very large is outsized, and swapping out for in gives the opposite

explanation.surface: A puzzled describer notes that a sharp slice sounds like the reverse of something huge.
explanation.walkthrough: Outsize means extra large, so its playful opposite would be in-sized.
explanation.definitionFit: Incised means sharply cut into a surface, as an engraving or a surgical incision is.

clue.text: A golf player

parts.note: surface reading: any golfer
setter's reading: a member of the Player family of golf, by first name

explanation.walkthrough: Gary Player is a South African golfer who won nine major championships; the clue asks for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous golfer Gary Player shares his surname with the ordinary word for a sportsman.

clue.text: Words to invoke the old divinities in the theatre?

definitions.text: Words to invoke the old divinities in the theatre

parts.words: Words to invoke the old divinities
parts.note: surface reading: an archaic exclamation calling on the deities
setter's reading: a call to the cheap seats in the highest gallery

explanation.walkthrough: The highest balcony of a theatre is nicknamed 'the gods', so an actor might address it in old-fashioned style.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mock-archaic exclamation of surprise addressing heavenly beings, and also suits the top gallery.

clue.text: Boast, they say, about someone from Zagreb

indicators.note: they say means the boast is taken as a spoken sound

parts.note: to crow is to boast
at as in occupied with, what you are about

explanation.surface: People brag about a person from the Croatian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'crow at' sounds like the answer. Zagreb is the capital of Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croat is a native of Croatia, whose capital city is Zagreb.

clue.text: Roundabout long since redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned means remade in a new pattern, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traffic circle that was rebuilt ages ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' suggests a road junction or fairground ride; here it means going all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enclosing surrounds another thing on every side, encircling it completely.

clue.text: Sanctity's sweet smell?

parts.note: surface reading: a fragrance belonging to holiness
setter's reading: the set phrase about a saintly reputation, of which this is the scent

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'in the odour of sanctity' is to be held in high regard for holiness; saints' bodies were said to give off a sweet perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a scent or smell, and it completes the phrase describing saintly repute.

clue.text: Follow the leftie at a gentle pace

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: Shadow a left-wing activist, walking slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy jogging gait like that of a dog, unhurried and steady.

clue.text: Cleaned up, as a parasite did

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wiped with a sponge

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the past-tense verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: lived off others' generosity

explanation.surface: A freeloading houseguest tidied up, as hangers-on do.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is both to wipe with a soft absorbent pad and to scrounge money or hospitality from others.

clue.text: Put on important hat for the races

parts.note: to don is to put on clothing
key means crucial
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Wear an impressive hat for a day at the horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: A donkey derby is a village fete event with races on donkeys, not the Epsom classic.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey derby is a series of comic races run on donkeys, typically at a fete or seaside.
